subject: Gideon
note: Evidence for Gideon's enhanced Bible figure page. Every quotation is in gideon.quotes.json and passes verify-quotes.mjs. Fetched texts are in design/saints-hub/sources/people/gideon/ (gitignored); the Fathers are the shared NPNF and ANF files. The Bible is the Berean Standard Bible (public domain); the chapters quoted are copied, verses joined, into bsb-gideon-chapters.txt.

life.text: Midian, the Amalekites and the people of the east raided Israel for seven years at harvest, 'like a great swarm of locusts'.

The angel of the LORD found Gideon, son of Joash the Abiezrite, threshing wheat in a winepress at Ophrah to hide it from Midian; the call, the complaint, 'my clan is the weakest in Manasseh', and 'Surely I will be with you'.
He asked for a sign; fire flared from the rock and consumed the offering; he built the altar The LORD Is Peace, which 'to this day' stood in Ophrah.

He tore down his father's altar to Baal and the Asherah pole with ten servants, by night, because he was afraid of his father's household and the men of the city; Joash defended him; he was named Jerubbaal, 'Let Baal contend with him'.
life.source: Judges 6:25-32 (BSB). The Christian Personality Test (site/src/data/personality.json, the Lookout) names him for Judges 6:15 and 27.

life.text: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him; he blew the ram's horn and called Abiezer, Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali. Many translations render the verb 'clothed'.
life.source: Judges 6:33-35 (BSB); parallel translations of Judges 6:34 at Bible Hub (biblehub-judges-6-34.txt). The 'clothed' tidbit was cut for space.

life.text: The fleece: dew on the fleece alone, a bowlful wrung out; then, asking God not to be angry, the fleece dry and the ground wet. Twice Gideon says 'as You have said'.
The army cut from 32,000 (22,000 went home, 10,000 remained) to the 300 who lapped; God's reason is Judges 7:2.
life.source: Judges 7:1-8 (BSB). The Catholic Encyclopedia (1909) and Sulpicius Severus (Sacred History 1.25, NPNF2 11) both give the total as 32,000.

life.text: The night visit with Purah, the barley loaf dream, the jars, torches and horns, 'A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!', and the rout.
Ephraim took Oreb and Zeeb and quarrelled with Gideon; his answer about the gleanings of Ephraim calmed them.
life.source: Judges 7:24 to 8:3 (BSB). Josephus, Antiquities 5.6 (Whiston): 'Gideon, as a man of temper, and that excelled in every virtue'.

life.text: The pursuit: Succoth and Penuel refused bread; 15,000 left at Karkor after 120,000 had fallen; Zebah and Zalmunna caught; Succoth punished, Penuel's tower pulled down and its men killed; the kings had killed his brothers at Tabor; Jether was too young to kill them.
life.source: Judges 8:4-21 (BSB). The tile's 135,000 is the sum of 8:10's two figures.

life.text: He refused to rule ('The LORD shall rule over you'), asked for gold earrings (1,700 shekels), made an ephod that became 'a snare to Gideon and his household'. Britannica calls it an idolatrous image; in Exodus 28 the ephod is a garment of the high priest.
life.source: Judges 8:22-27 (BSB); Exodus 28:4-6; Britannica, 'Gideon' (britannica-gideon.txt): 'he fashioned an idolatrous image from the booty'.

life.text: Forty years of rest; seventy sons, many wives; a concubine in Shechem bore Abimelech; he died at a ripe old age and was buried in Joash's tomb at Ophrah; Israel turned back to the Baals.
Abimelech killed the seventy 'on one stone'; Jotham escaped and told the fable of the trees; Abimelech reigned three years and was killed at Thebez by a millstone dropped by a woman.

names.text: Gideon comes from the Hebrew for 'cut down' (Catholic Encyclopedia: 'hewer'); Jerubbaal is 'Baal will contend' / 'let Baal contend'; Jerubbesheth (2 Samuel 11:21) is 'shame will contend'; Abimelech is 'father is king'.
names.source: Strong's Hebrew 1439, 3378, 3380, 40 with Brown-Driver-Briggs, at Bible Hub (strongs-hebrew-*.txt); Catholic Encyclopedia (1909), 'Gideon' ('Gideon or Gedeon (Hebrew "hewer")').
names.note: Gedeon is the form in the Catholic Encyclopedia and the 1916 Roman Martyrology.

said_and_read.text: Other Bible writers remember him: 1 Samuel 12:11 (Jerubbaal), Isaiah 9:4 and 10:26 ('the day of Midian', 'the rock of Oreb'), Psalm 83:11, Hebrews 11:32-33.
Chrysostom answers those who fault Hebrews for naming Barak, Samson and Jephthah: 'do not tell me of the rest of their life, but only whether they did not believe and shine in Faith'.

The fleece as Israel and the nations: Irenaeus (the fleece 'a type of the people'; the dew the Spirit, later 'diffused throughout all the earth'); Augustine (grace 'hidden in a cloud, as the rain in the fleece'; 'the whole world, like that floor, is full of grace').
said_and_read.source: Irenaeus, Against Heresies 3.17 (ANF 1, shared/anf01.txt); Augustine, Sermon 81 on the New Testament (Ben. 131), NPNF1 6 (shared/npnf106.txt; the brief lists npnf106 as Jerome, but the volume is Augustine).

said_and_read.text: Ambrose, On the Holy Spirit (381), Book 1 opens with Gideon: asking twice was not doubt ('He was not then doubtful, but careful that we should not doubt'); Concerning Widows 3 joins Psalm 72:6 ('shall come down like rain upon a fleece') to Gideon's fleece.
said_and_read.source: NPNF2 10 (shared/npnf210.txt); the date 381 is from the NPNF introduction to the two treatises.

said_and_read.text: Mary and the fleece: the OCA's life of Gideon quotes Ode 9 of the second canon of the Entry of the Theotokos (the radiant cloud, dew upon the fleece); the Akathist hails the Virgin as the fleece Gideon foresaw. Both are modern copyrighted translations, so the page paraphrases them and quotes neither. Cyril of Jerusalem (Catechetical Lecture 12.9) reads Psalm 72:6's fleece as Christ's humanity.
said_and_read.source: oca-righteous-gideon.txt; sanidopoulos-gideon.txt (a lead: his own translation of the Akathist line); shared/npnf207.txt.

said_and_read.text: The lapping read both ways: Gregory of Nazianzus, 'the three hundred men with Gideon, who bravely lapped'; Josephus, the lappers drank 'tumultuously' and 'out of fear', and those were the 300.
said_and_read.source: Gregory of Nazianzus, Oration 42 (NPNF2 7, shared/npnf207.txt); Josephus, Antiquities 5.6.3 (Whiston, josephus-antiquities-5.txt).

said_and_read.text: The Gideons: founded by three travelling salesmen at Janesville, Wisconsin, 1 July 1899; Bibles placed from November 1908; the emblem a two-handled pitcher and torch, for Gideon's victory.
said_and_read.source: Britannica, 'Gideons International' (britannica-gideons-international.txt); gideons.org/about (gideons-about.txt): the name chosen in 1899, first hotel Bible order 1908.
said_and_read.note: The Gideons' own statement of why they chose the name (quoted on other sites) was not found on their current site, so the page does not quote it.

feasts.text: 1916 Roman Martyrology, 1 September: 'In Palestine, the Saints Josue and Gedeon.'
feasts.note: The page paraphrases it and does not print 'Saint' beside his name (the Old Testament rule).

feasts.text: Not in the calendar used at Mass today.
Greek synaxarion: 26 September, 'Ὁ Ἅγιος Γεδεῶν ὁ Δίκαιος'.
Coptic synaxarium: 16 Kiahk, 'The Departure of the Righteous Gideon, One of the Judges of Israel'; 16 Kiahk is 25 December (26 December in the year before a Gregorian leap year).

pictures.text: Band: Gideon, detail of the head, wall painting in the drum of the dome, Church of the Panagia tou Arakou (Arakos), Lagoudera, Cyprus. Photograph by the Byzantine Institute staff, 1968 to 1973, Dumbarton Oaks MSBZ004_BF_S_1979_1997D. Commons licence tag {{Cc-zero}}. 5198 x 3424 on Commons; cropped from x = 600 (dropping the blue ground at the left), resized to 1800 x 1340, JPEG quality 80, 346 KB. posM 100% 40%, posD 62% 40% (face at about 64% across, 40% down).
pictures.source: Commons file page and API; the date 1192 from the church's dedicatory inscription as given by Wikipedia, 'Panagia tou Araka' (a lead: 'completed in December 1192').

pictures.text: Second picture: La Toison de Gédéon, Nicolas Dipre (died 1532), about 1500, Musée du Petit Palais, Avignon, Inv 22875. Commons licence tag {{PD-Art|PD-old-auto-expired|deathyear=1532}}. 1058 x 1280, saved whole (the frame's inscriptions are part of the picture: VELLUS GEDEONIS IUDICUM above, Psalm 71:6 of the Vulgate below). 308 KB.
pictures.source: Commons file page and API; the inscriptions read from the file.
pictures.note: Below the brief's 1500 px: the Commons original is 1058 x 1280.

pictures.text: Not used: the Kirillo-Belozersky iconostasis icon (it is the personality test's face); Doré's plate (gideon.jpg). Considered: Heemskerck's Gideon (Strasbourg, about 1550, a wing that once flanked a lost picture of the Virgin; only 964 px wide), Eeckhout's The Angel and Gideon (small figures), a 17th-century North Russian icon.

could_not_verify: The modern Roman Martyrology's day for Gideon (Wikipedia says 26 September, with 'citation needed'): not checked, left off.
The Armenian Church's 30 July (Wikipedia, unsourced): left off.
Whether the Orthodox name Gideon in the services of the Sundays of the Forefathers: not checked, left off.
The Gideons' own words on why they took his name: not found on their site, left off.

checker_2026_09_25.by: One light checking pass (Moses, Gideon, John the Baptist), 2026-09-25
checked: Every number against the BSB: 7 years (Judges 6:1), 32,000 / 22,000 / 10,000 / 300 (7:3-7), 120,000 + 15,000 (8:10), 1,700 shekels (8:26), 70 sons (8:30), 40 years of rest (8:28), Abimelech's 3 years (9:22).

Feasts read in the texts: 1916 Martyrology 1 September 'In Palestine, the Saints Josue and Gedeon'; synaxarion.gr 26 September; OCA 'Commemorated on November 26'; Coptic 16 Kiahk 'The Departure of the Righteous Gideon'; nothing for him in the LSB.

Attributions: Josephus 'a man of temper' and the lappers drinking 'tumultuously' 'out of fear' (Antiquities 5); Chrysostom's Homily 27 on Hebrews answers those who 'find fault with Paul' for naming Barak, Samson and Jephthah; the OCA quotes Ode 9 of the Entry canon; Britannica calls the ephod 'an idolatrous image'; Britannica on the Gideons (1899, three travelling salesmen, pitcher and torch); Strong's 40 gives 'father is king'.
Disputes: the reason for the 300 is told both ways (Gregory of Nazianzus, Josephus) with no winner; the fleece readings each in their own words.
Rules: capitals, no 'St Gideon', no section marks, italics; licences read on Commons (Cc-zero; PD-Art|PD-old-auto-expired); sizes match; Doré's gideon.jpg untouched.

changed: Feasts note: it said churches on the old calendar keep 'each date' 13 days later, which would move the Coptic date too. Now: the Greek and OCA dates move 13 days; the Coptic 16 Kiahk falls on 26 December in the year before a leap year.
Circle, Abimelech: 'He died when a woman dropped a millstone on his head' now follows Judges 9:53-54: the millstone, then his armour-bearer ran him through.
The angel moment: Gideon's quoted answer now starts with a capital ('If the LORD is with us').
for_owner: The writer's open questions stand: the Byzantine band (posM 100% 40%, worth a look at 390), the Dipre panel below 1500 px, the fleece section, and the plainly told pursuit.
